title: Control Plane Responsibility Atlas
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a concise, operational-first map of control plane responsibilities and ownership for API gateway, orchestration, and runtime adapters across multi-region deployments. Goal: reduce ambiguity during incidents and design reviews by making handoffs explicit (who owns what, and where routing/decision logic lives).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: control plane components that make routing, rollout, and runtime selection decisions (API gateway, smart router, policy engine, orchestration service, runtime adapters, model-catalog interface, multi-region coordinator).
- Out of scope: compute-side runtime implementation details (exact kernel implementations, per-GPU scheduling internals), client SDKs, and billing pipelines (these have separate owners but are linked).

High-level principles:
1) Single source of truth: control-plane config (routes, policies, model pins, rollouts) is stored in the Control Configstore (see linked Confluence page) and is the authoritative input for all region controllers.
2) Fail open with constraints: in a partial-control-plane outage, replicas should prefer degraded but safe behavior (route to compatible model-variant with stricter rate limits) rather than drop traffic.
3) Locality-first routing with regional fallbacks: prefer same-region runtime; fall back to cross-region only when policy permits and latency budget allows.
4) Ownership by responsibility, not by hostname: teams own behaviors (e.g., rate-limiting policy decisions) across tiers rather than single endpoints.

Service ownership roster (component -> primary responsibility -> owner):
- API Gateway: authentication, authorization, edge rate-limits, per-tenant quotas enforcement, initial request validation, request tagging (route/tenant/trace). Owner: eng-platform-gateway.
- Smart Router (control-plane routing engine): route selection (model variant, region, capacity tier), capacity-aware placement decisions, fallback chain evaluation. Owner: eng-platform-routing.
- Policy Engine: evaluation of fine-grained routing rules (SLAs, customer-specified pins, allowlists), feature flag gating for rollout behavior. Owner: eng-platform-engineering (policy subteam).
- Orchestration Service (control-plane lifecycle): deploys model slices to runtime adapters, rollout strategies (canary/A-B/gradual), autoscale commands (desired replica counts). Owner: eng-orchestration.
- Runtime Adapters (region-level): translate routing decisions into runtime-specific actions (start/stop containers, allocate GPU pools, apply quantization profile). Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Model Catalog API: version metadata, compatible runtime variant metadata (quantization, memory profile), deprecation signals. Owner: eng-models (applied-ml).
- KV/Prefix Cache Manager (control-plane coord): global cache invalidation policy, mapping of cached prefixes to runtime owners, cache warming recommendations. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (cache team).
- Telemetry & Tracing Pipeline (control-plane sidecar): ingest control-plane and route-level metrics, expose per-route latency/cost breakdowns. Owner: eng-observability.
- Audit & Compliance Store: immutable action logs for pin/rollout/route changes, access controls, retention policy. Owner: security-and-compliance.
- Multi-region Coordinator: config propagation, leader election for region mastership, conflict resolution rules for concurrent updates. Owner: eng-platform-engineering (multi-region subteam).

Routing policy primitives (what lives where):
- Route selection logic: Smart Router (control-plane) evaluates list of compatible runtime variants then scores by latency, cost, and affinity.
- Affinity rules: stored as part of tenant config in Control Configstore; enforced by Smart Router (region affinity), API Gateway (sticky session hints).
- Fallback chains: policy engine defines ordered fallbacks (same-variant different region, cheaper quantized variant, lower-priority dedicated pool). Fallback execution is orchestrated by Smart Router.
- Capacity-aware routing: runtime adapters publish capacity tokens; Smart Router uses soft and hard limits to avoid overcommit.

Multi-region behaviours and invariants:
- Control Configstore is multi-master read/write with CRDT-based last-writer-wins for non-critical routing hints; critical ops (rollout toggles, SLA changes) use single-leader write with optimistic locking.
- Propagation window target: 30s for config changes to reach all active region controllers under normal conditions; alerts if >2min.
- Leader election: Multi-region Coordinator elects a region master for cross-region global operations (e.g., global canary that needs synchronous cutover).
- Region failover: Smart Router prefers local runtimes; if regional outage detected, route to next-best region but only after passing latency and data residency checks.

API Gateway specific responsibilities:
- Edge auth + tenant identification (api keys/jwt verification).
- Quick-reject decisions for invalid requests before hitting routing pipeline.
- Rate-limit enforcement windows (burst vs sustained); owner must maintain default policies and tenant override API.
- Request enrichment (add trace headers, tenant metadata) before forwarding to Smart Router.

Orchestration responsibilities (lifecycle & rollouts):
- Model deploy lifecycle: validate model artifact against catalog (compatibility matrix), stage to canary region, monitor quality signals (eval hooks), promote or rollback.
- Autoscaling signals: accept telemetry-derived signals from runtime adapters and apply binning rules; preserve capacity buffers for SLA-bound tenants.
- Canary semantics: default canary size=1% of traffic for hosted API, configurable per-tenant.

Runtime adapter invariants and contracts:
- Runtime adapter exposes: health endpoint, capacity tokens, supported-variant list, KV cache ownership hints, telemetry endpoint.
- Any change to adapter API is a breaking change and requires a deprecation window and coordinated rollout.
- Adapter is responsible for ensuring model pinning (if requested) holds until orchestration confirms migration.

SLOs, Alerts, and Escalation:
- Control Plane availability SLO: 99.95% regional, 99.9% global for critical path (authentication + routing).
- Route latency budget: control-plane decision time < 50ms P95 under normal load; alert at >150ms P95.
- Canary health alerts: automatic rollback on model-quality regressions (>3x baseline error rate within 1h).
- Pager paths: eng-platform-routing -> eng-orchestration -> eng-serving-runtime depending on signal type. Ownership handbook (oncall rotations) lives in eng-platform engineering handbook.

Change process and governance:
- Any routing-policy change requires: design doc PR, staging test run (multi-region if global), and a rollout playbook entry.
- Minor config changes (rate limits, thresholds) can be submitted via change API with automatic audit log entry; major behavioral changes require a design review and cross-team signoff.
- Emergency quickfixes must be documented post-mortem and traced to a Jira ticket.

Open questions / action items:
- Decide exact semantics for cross-region data residency enforcement (legal vs latency tradeoffs). Owner: security-and-compliance + eng-platform-engineering.
- Finalize the format for capacity token exchange between adapters and Smart Router (binary vs JSON push). Owner: eng-serving-runtime. Action: prototype by 2025-03-01.
- Define default canary thresholds for Dedicated vs Hosted customers (business input needed). Owner: product-hosted-api + customer-success.

Next steps:
- Ship a short ‘ownership cheatsheet’ derived from this doc to oncall Slack and embed in runbooks. (Owner: Maya Chen, due 2025-02-20)
- Add missing telemetry gauges for propagation window and per-route fallback counts (Owner: eng-observability, due 2025-03-10).

Notes and references:
- See linked Confluence page for diagrams and sequence flows.
- Related tickets: PLAT-482 (multi-region coordinator design), PLAT-501 (smart router capacity API).

Document history:
- 2024-11-05 created (initial mapping)
- 2025-01-12 added multi-region coordinator details
- 2025-02-10 review updates and added action items

If you're reviewing: call out any missing owner or ambiguous handoff. This is intended to be operationally prescriptive — if a team can't accept an item, mark it as RACI-Disagree and propose a remap.
